greetings.speaker: SFKast
greetings.text: Mind the cables. Some of them are load bearing, and none of them are labeled.

greetings.speaker: SFKast
greetings.text: Ah. The visitor security keeps radioing about. Come, we should talk.

greetings.speaker: SFKast
greetings.text: That device on your back. I believe it still has our inventory number on it.

greetings.speaker: SFKast
greetings.text: Dr. Hale is in the Test Chamber. Follow the shouting.

greetings.speaker: SFKast
greetings.text: Rusk has been pacing again. If he asks you for anything, use discretion.

greetings.speaker: SFKast
greetings.text: You have the look of someone who's been reading. Rusk's handwriting, I suppose.

greetings.speaker: SFKast
greetings.text: Clearance suits you. Try not to abuse it more than the rest of us do.

greetings.speaker: SFKast
greetings.text: Most of the staff sleep at this hour. I find the crater more honest at night.

greetings.speaker: SFHale
greetings.text: You hear that hum? That's the array. Beautiful, isn't it?

greetings.speaker: SFHale
greetings.text: My manipulator! You've been taking care of her? Don't answer, I can see the scorch marks.

greetings.speaker: SFHale
greetings.text: How's the pull on her? Lifting carts yet? Tell me you've thrown a cow.

greetings.speaker: SFHale
greetings.text: Kast sent you? Good. I need hands, and you have two.

greetings.speaker: SFHale
greetings.text: Those crystals sang beautifully. Rusk wants a word with you, by the way.

greetings.speaker: SFHale
greetings.text: Clearance, eh? Then I'm officially allowed to sell you dangerous things.

greetings.speaker: SFHale
greetings.text: You'd look better holding a manipulator. Everyone would.

greetings.speaker: SFRusk
greetings.text: Did you close the door behind you? Please tell me you closed the door.

greetings.speaker: SFRusk
greetings.text: Wash your hands before touching anything. And after. Especially after.

greetings.speaker: SFRusk
greetings.text: Crystals for Hale? Wear gloves. They hum right through the skin.

greetings.speaker: SFRusk
greetings.text: You still have the keycard? Keep it out of sight. Kast notices things.

greetings.speaker: SFRusk
greetings.text: I've told you everything. I feel lighter, and also terribly exposed.

greetings.speaker: SFRusk
greetings.text: The truth is out. Strange. The air in here tastes cleaner.

greetings.speaker: SFRusk
greetings.text: I don't sleep much anymore. The vents make noises at night.

greetings.speaker: SFVenn
greetings.text: If you came to report a broken thing, take a number. The number is also broken.

greetings.speaker: SFVenn
greetings.text: Do you know where a man finds a decent wrench in this province? No? Nobody does.

greetings.speaker: SFVenn
greetings.text: Is that Hale's toy? Don't let him near it. He'll want to tune it.

greetings.speaker: SFVenn
greetings.text: Fetching crystals for Hale? Bring a spare. I need one for the lights.

greetings.speaker: SFVenn
greetings.text: So it's all coming out about Wing B. I rewired those doors. Never asked why.

greetings.speaker: SFVenn
greetings.text: Clearance means you can use the good lift. It still squeaks, mind you.

greetings.speaker: SFVenn
greetings.text: Sun's out. The solar collector will work for nearly an hour.

greetings.speaker: SFPell
greetings.text: Oh! Sorry. I thought you were... sorry. Hello.

greetings.speaker: SFPell
greetings.text: I haven't slept since Tirdas. Or the Tirdas before. Hard to say.

greetings.speaker: SFPell
greetings.text: Looking for the Director? Up the stairs. Please don't tell him I'm on break.

greetings.speaker: SFPell
greetings.text: Is that the missing prototype? Could you point it somewhere else, please?

greetings.speaker: SFPell
greetings.text: People are whispering about Wing B. I don't want to whisper. I want to be elsewhere.

greetings.speaker: SFPell
greetings.text: You confronted the Director and walked out? Impressive. Truly.

greetings.speaker: SFHolt
greetings.text: Brennic Holt. Remember the name. It'll be on the Test Chamber door someday.

greetings.speaker: SFHolt
greetings.text: If you're looking for real talent around here, you just found it.

greetings.speaker: SFHolt
greetings.text: Hale's gun. Honestly, I'd have built it with a better grip.

greetings.speaker: SFHolt
greetings.text: Running errands for Hale? Starting at the bottom. I respect that.

greetings.speaker: SFHolt
greetings.text: Rumor says Kast is in trouble. Shame. Promotions open up in times like these.

greetings.speaker: SFHolt
greetings.text: Clearance already? Fine. I'm only slightly jealous.

greetings.speaker: SFMire
greetings.text: Good day. Have you read any local sagas? I'm halfway through one about a bear.

greetings.speaker: SFMire
greetings.text: Do the stars look the same where you're from? They don't, where I'm from.

greetings.speaker: SFMire
greetings.text: Lovely morning. The Nords at the crater's edge waved at me today.

greetings.speaker: SFMire
greetings.text: You're new here. Welcome. Don't touch anything that glows green.

greetings.speaker: SFMire
greetings.text: You carry that thing like a farmer carries a hoe. It's oddly comforting.

greetings.speaker: SFMire
greetings.text: I knew some of the people in Wing B. Nobody would tell us anything.

greetings.speaker: SFMoran
greetings.text: Keep your hands where my officers can see them.

greetings.speaker: SFMoran
greetings.text: Another civilian. Wonderful. Don't touch the scientists, they bruise.

greetings.speaker: SFMoran
greetings.text: Director's expecting you. Straight through, no detours.

greetings.speaker: SFMoran
greetings.text: Kast will want that back. Not my problem unless you point it at my people.

greetings.speaker: SFMoran
greetings.text: Wing B. They sealed it on my shift and told me it was empty.

greetings.speaker: SFMoran
greetings.text: Your clearance came through. Armory's open to you. Don't make me regret it.

greetings.speaker: SFMoran
greetings.text: Night shift. Keep your torch low and your voice lower.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: Move along. Nothing to see. Well, plenty to see. Just don't.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: Six months in a crater. I used to have a window.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: You from around here? Is it always this cold, or is it just us?

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: Hear that? No? Good. Neither did I.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: The scientists break it, we shoot it. That's the arrangement.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: Some Nord offered me a bottle of mead for my helmet. I almost said yes.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: Careful with that manipulator. Last fellow who dropped one lost a toe.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: Captain says you've got clearance. Doesn't mean I have to like it.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: If you see something with legs and no face, tell someone. Loudly.

greetings.speaker: GuardA
greetings.text: Sun's out. So it's only freezing, instead of very freezing.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: Hey. Don't wander off the lit paths. We don't go there either.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: I'd give a week's pay for a proper hot meal. Everything here is soup.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: Was that a dragon earlier? Tell me that wasn't a dragon.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: The scientists say it's safe. The scientists said that last time.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: Heard the truth about Wing B. Makes you wonder who's next on the list.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: Twelve hour shifts and the pay comes in promises. Living the dream.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: Quiet night. I hate quiet nights.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: A giant walked past the fence yesterday. Didn't even look at us. Rude.

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: Is that Hale's gun? Does the Captain know you have that?

greetings.speaker: GuardB
greetings.text: Checkpoint's that way. Keep your weapon sheathed and your manners polite.

idle.speaker: SFKast
idle.text: Variance at four percent. Acceptable. Probably.

idle.speaker: SFKast
idle.text: Someone has moved my chair. Again.

idle.speaker: SFKast
idle.text: The Directorate expects results. The Directorate is also very far away.

idle.speaker: SFKast
idle.text: Remarkable stone. Utterly indifferent to our deadlines.

idle.speaker: SFKast
idle.text: If Hale pushes that array once more without asking, he'll be counting rivets.

idle.speaker: SFHale
idle.text: Come on, sweetheart, give me ten more percent.

idle.speaker: SFHale
idle.text: Who keeps unplugging the capacitor? I know it's Venn.

idle.speaker: SFHale
idle.text: Gravity's just a suggestion, if you ask it nicely.

idle.speaker: SFHale
idle.text: One more test. Just one more. Then lunch.

idle.speaker: SFHale
idle.text: I need more crystals. I always need more crystals.

idle.speaker: SFRusk
idle.text: The specimen moved again. It isn't supposed to do that.

idle.speaker: SFRusk
idle.text: Note to self: stop naming the headcrabs.

idle.speaker: SFRusk
idle.text: Dosage, dosage... where did I write the dosage?

idle.speaker: SFRusk
idle.text: Something scratched the vent last night. I'm sure of it.

idle.speaker: SFRusk
idle.text: Nobody listens until it's too late. Then everybody listens.

idle.speaker: SFVenn
idle.text: My kingdom for a roll of proper tape.

idle.speaker: SFVenn
idle.text: These locals forge swords like artists and can't make a single screw.

idle.speaker: SFVenn
idle.text: Generator two is humming in a key I don't like.

idle.speaker: SFVenn
idle.text: If it sparks, it's fine. If it stops sparking, run.

idle.speaker: SFVenn
idle.text: I fixed that yesterday. Why is it broken? Who touched it?

idle.speaker: SFPell
idle.text: Calibrate, log, calibrate, log... I dream in logs now.

idle.speaker: SFPell
idle.text: Was that a noise? That was definitely a noise.

idle.speaker: SFPell
idle.text: Please work. Please work. Oh good, it worked.

idle.speaker: SFPell
idle.text: I should have stayed in theoretical studies.

idle.speaker: SFPell
idle.text: Holt took credit for my numbers again. Of course he did.

idle.speaker: SFHolt
idle.text: Senior Researcher Holt. Has a nice ring to it.

idle.speaker: SFHolt
idle.text: Hale's methods are sloppy. I'd have finished this weeks ago.

idle.speaker: SFHolt
idle.text: Where are those readings? Does anyone here work except me?

idle.speaker: SFHolt
idle.text: If I'd built the manipulator, it would fold up for travel.

idle.speaker: SFHolt
idle.text: Note: pitch my idea to the Director. Before Hale steals it.

idle.speaker: SFMire
idle.text: Ysgramor sailed from Atmora, and nobody wrote down why he left. Same as us.

idle.speaker: SFMire
idle.text: Sweetrolls. I still don't know what makes them so sweet. I've asked.

idle.speaker: SFMire
idle.text: I wonder what my sister is doing right now.

idle.speaker: SFMire
idle.text: The innkeeper in Riverwood called me 'friend.' Nice word.

idle.speaker: SFMire
idle.text: Nords sing when they're sad. Maybe I should try that.

idle.speaker: SFMoran
idle.text: Eyes up. Something's always watching from that ridge.

idle.speaker: SFMoran
idle.text: Somebody's armor isn't regulation. I'll find you.

idle.speaker: SFMoran
idle.text: Scientists. Can't protect them from themselves.

idle.speaker: SFMoran
idle.text: Fence line held last night. Small miracles.

idle.speaker: SFMoran
idle.text: Who left the canister bay unlocked? I'll find out.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: Fourteen hours on. Ten to go. Lovely.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: I swear that rock just moved.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: Who decided white coats were a good idea in a crater?

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: If one more scientist calls me 'officer person,' I'm quitting.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: Smells like ozone and wet dog. Every single day.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: Wish I'd brought a warmer coat. Or a warmer world.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: Note to self: never volunteer for anything ever again.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: That's the third canister this week. Who's counting? Me.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: Somewhere a bard is singing about me. Probably badly.

idle.speaker: GuardA
idle.text: Quiet. Too quiet. I hate it when I say that.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: Whistling past the crater. Totally calm. Totally fine.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: Remember when the worst job was gate duty? Still is.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: The locals think we're mages. I've stopped correcting them.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: My boots haven't been dry since the day we got here.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: Headcrab in the mess hall again? No, wait. Just the stew.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: Hey, crater. Do something interesting. Actually, don't.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: I could use a drink. Not mead. Anything but mead.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: One more patrol and I'm sitting down. Captain or no Captain.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: Saw a fox chewing on a crystal. Fox seemed fine. I'm worried.

idle.speaker: GuardB
idle.text: Somebody tell that generator to stop groaning.

combat.speaker: GuardA
combat.text: Back to the Hollow with you!

combat.speaker: GuardA
combat.text: It bit me! It actually bit me!

combat.speaker: GuardA
combat.text: Clear. I think. Check it twice.

combat.speaker: GuardA
combat.text: I'm not paid enough for this!

combat.speaker: GuardA
combat.text: Lost sight of it! Spread out!

combat.speaker: GuardB
combat.text: Go back where you came from!

combat.speaker: GuardB
combat.text: Ugh, I felt that through the armor.

combat.speaker: GuardB
combat.text: Clear. Somebody check my helmet for crabs.

combat.speaker: GuardB
combat.text: That's the last of them. Hopefully.

combat.speaker: GuardB
combat.text: Somebody tell the Captain. We lost one.

combat.speaker: GuardB
combat.text: Lost it. Keep your eyes sharp.

combat.speaker: SFMoran
combat.text: Put it down and keep it down!

combat.speaker: SFKast
combat.text: I'll be in my office. Locked.

combat.speaker: SFKast
combat.text: Security will handle this. Not me.

combat.speaker: SFHale
combat.text: Oh, that's a big one! Where's my manipulator?

combat.speaker: SFHale
combat.text: I'll come back with something bigger!

combat.speaker: SFRusk
combat.text: I'm hurt... where are my gloves?

combat.speaker: SFRusk
combat.text: I knew this would happen! I knew it!

combat.speaker: SFVenn
combat.text: Oh, great. Something else to fix.

combat.speaker: SFVenn
combat.text: Ow! Watch the hands, I need those!

combat.speaker: SFVenn
combat.text: Ugh. Worse than a live wire.

combat.speaker: SFVenn
combat.text: I'll be hiding in the generator room.

combat.speaker: SFHolt
combat.text: Get it away from the equipment!

combat.speaker: SFHolt
combat.text: I'm far too valuable for this!

combat.speaker: SFMire
combat.text: By the Nine! That's what they say, right? By the Nine!

lines.text: You pushed the array to ninety percent last night.
Ninety two. And nothing exploded. You're welcome.
Nothing exploded this time. The logs are not a dare, Marcus.
Then stop writing them like one.
Give me one full cycle at peak resonance. Just one.
The last full cycle gave us Incident Seven.
That was containment. My chamber held fine.
How comforting for your chamber.
Rusk says you sealed Wing B with people inside. Tell me he's lying.
Rusk is many things. A liar is not one of them.
I built half this place for you, Aurelius.
And I kept the other half standing. Pick which half you'd rather lose.
Venn, I need the capacitor bank at full charge by noon.
And I need a screwdriver that isn't a sharpened spoon.
So can you do it?
Of course I can do it. I'm just going to complain the whole time.
I put in for copper wire. Three weeks ago.
The supply rift is unreliable. You know this.
So I traded a Riverwood smith for some. He wanted a lantern.
You gave a local our technology?
I gave him a lantern, Director. It's a lantern.
The specimens react to the array cycles. Every single time.
Correlation, Emil. Not causation.
They turn toward the Test Chamber. All of them. At once.
Then write it up. Quietly.
Emil! Want to see a crystal sing at eighty percent?
I'd rather see it sleep at zero.
Where's your sense of wonder?
In Wing B. Behind a sealed door.
Doctor, are you all right? You've barely eaten.
I keep dreaming about the vents, Ollan.
My grandmother said bad dreams are just the mind cleaning house.
Then my house is very, very dirty.
Did you hear? Hale singed his eyebrows off again.
Again? That's the third time this month.
If I ran the chamber, nobody would lose any eyebrows.
You'd make me run the chamber, and I'd lose mine.
Delegation, Jory. It's a leadership skill.
Do you think there were people in Wing B when it sealed?
The roster said it was empty. Rosters don't lie.
Rosters get written by people, Ollan.
Let's not talk about it here.
You actually read those Nord books? They're all about axes.
Not all of them. Some are about bears. And honor.
Honor won't calibrate a resonance array.
Neither will you, from what Hale says.
Mister Venn, the light in my lab keeps flickering.
Does it flicker, or does it strobe?
Is there a difference?
One is annoying. The other means move your desk. Now.
A woman in Riverwood lit a candle with her finger today.
With what? A flint up her sleeve?
Nothing. Just her finger.
Great. They get free fire, and I can't even get a fuse.
Two more canisters spotted near the north ridge.
Retrieve them. Discreetly.
My people aren't hounds, Director. They bleed.
Then send the ones who bleed least.
I'll pretend you didn't say that.
You told me Wing B was empty.
I told you what you needed to hold the line.
My officers were on that door. They heard the knocking.
So did I, Captain. So did I.
Listen up. Headcrabs like the ventilation. Check the grates every hour.
Every hour, Captain? They're very small grates.
And very small headcrabs fit through them. Every hour.
Nobody fraternizes with the locals while on duty.
What about off duty, Captain?
Off duty, you sleep. That's an order.
Understood. Sleep. Not mead.
If a scientist tells you something is safe, what do you do?
Assume it isn't, Captain.
And if they say it's dangerous?
Run, Captain.
Good. You'll outlive most of them.
You ever think about going home?
Every day. Twice before breakfast.
Think they'll ever open the rift for a ride back?
They can't even open the canteen on time.
Saw a dragon over the mountains this morning.
A real one?
No, a painted one. Yes, a real one.
And we're guarding a giant glowing crater. Perfect.
Tried the mead in Riverwood on my day off.
And?
Woke up in a barn. Next to a goat. Wearing my helmet.
The goat, or you?
I'd rather not say.
Holt asked me to carry his notes. His notes.
Did you?
I carried them. Straight into the brazier.
Officer of the month.
What's worse, a headcrab or a zombie?
Headcrab. A zombie's just a headcrab with a commute.
I really didn't need that picture in my head.
You hear what Rusk found? About Wing B?
Everyone's heard. The Director sealed it with people inside.
And we stood guard while they knocked.
We didn't know. Keep telling yourself that. I do.
There's a giant herding mammoths near the north fence.
Did it notice us?
It waved.
Should we have waved back?
I did. Seemed polite.
Dr. Hale, I reviewed your calibration notes. I have suggestions.
Have you built anything that can lift a cart, Holt?
Not yet.
Then your suggestions can wait in line behind the cart.
Pell! Readings on crystal four?
It's humming at a pitch I can taste, sir.
Excellent! Write that down. Exactly that.
Taste, sir?
Science is a full body experience, Jory.
The crater floor sank another inch this month.
Is that structural, or is something underneath?
I'm an engineer. I only answer the first kind of question.
Then who answers the second kind?
Mire, I hear you've been visiting Riverwood.
Only to trade, Director. And to read at the inn.
Say nothing about the site. The locals already think we're star cultists.
They also call me 'the polite one.' I'd hate to ruin that.
Doctor, is it true? The journal, the people in Wing B?
It's true, Jory. I should have spoken sooner.
Why didn't you?
Fear. The same reason you're whispering now.
So Kast is still in charge after all that?
The Directorate is far away. And nobody knows the array like him.
Except you.
Except me. And I'm the one who kept pushing it.
If Kast falls, Hale moves up, and someone gets the chamber.
People died, Brennic.
I know. I'm sorry. I just don't know what else to think about.
Doc, one of my officers got scratched by a crab.
Scratched or bitten? It matters enormously.
Scratched.
Then send them in. And keep them away from anything with legs.
Do you miss home, officer?
Every hour. You?
I miss rain that doesn't turn into snow.
I miss being warm. I've forgotten what it feels like.
Venn, the main gate is stuck again.
Did you kick it?
Yes.
Kick it lower. That's the whole repair.

responses.text: Starfall Research Site. We study the crystal that fell here a year ago.
We are the Lambda Directorate. Scholars, mostly. Far from home, entirely.
Far enough that the answer would mean nothing to you.
Let's leave it at that.
The star struck hard enough to melt the bedrock into glass.
Its heart was a crystal that stores energy from nothing. Zero-point energy.

children.speaker: SFKast
children.prompt: Energy from nothing? Sounds like magic.

responses.text: Your mages would say so. We prefer equations. They're less temperamental.

topics.speaker: SFKast
topics.prompt: What do you think of your staff?

responses.text: Hale is brilliant and reckless. Rusk is careful and frightened.
Venn keeps the lights on. The juniors keep me humble, mostly by breaking things.
Fauna from the Hollow, a neighboring space our experiments brushed against.
The parasites are called headcrabs. Unpleasant, but manageable. Mostly.

topics.speaker: SFKast
topics.prompt: What do you make of Skyrim?

responses.text: A province of shouting men, flying lizards, and alarmingly good mead.
I admire the Nords. They solve problems with confidence, if not accuracy.
A containment fault in Wing B. Regrettable. Resolved.
Let's not dwell on it. Rumor makes a poor scientist.
I run the Test Chamber. Crystals go in, wonders come out.
Sometimes sparks come out. Sometimes the wonders come out sideways.
The Zero-Point Field Manipulator. My masterpiece. Pulls, pushes, and hurls like a dancer.
Well. A dancer with a very strong grip.
The crystal is the heart. Every pull borrows energy from the field.
Feed it crystals, and it'll love you back.
A junior panicked after Incident Seven and ran off with a prototype.
Smart kid, honestly. Picked the best one.

topics.speaker: SFHale
topics.prompt: What do you think of Director Kast?

responses.text: Aurelius is the smartest man I know. Also the most cautious, which is a waste.
He wants the array at half power. Half! Like eating half a sweetroll.
A border world. Ours rubs up against it when the crystals resonate.
Gray light, no wind, and things that think we're dinner. Fascinating place.
Love it. Dragons! Actual dragons! Do you know the lift on those wings?
I've been trying to get a dragon scale under the lens for months.
Xenobiology. The parasites from the Hollow, mostly. How they feed, how they bond.
I used to find it fascinating. Now I mostly find it in my nightmares.
They latch onto the head and fuse with the nervous system.
The host keeps walking. Keeps groaning. Whether anyone's still inside, I can't say.
I've tried. Every time. I'm sorry, the answer is no.
Aim for the parasite, not the host. And keep your head covered.

topics.speaker: SFRusk
topics.prompt: What do you think of Kast?

responses.text: The Director is brilliant. And he keeps secrets the way others keep pets.
Carefully. Lovingly. Behind locked doors.
I study things that climb into people's skulls. Of course I'm frightened.
The only sane people here are the frightened ones.
I can't talk about that. Not here. Not yet.
I keep the resonance array from shaking itself apart. And the generators. And the lights.
If it works, that's me. If it doesn't, that's also me, apparently.
This province has a thousand ways to sharpen a sword and zero ways to make a bolt.
I traded a smith a lantern for copper wire. He thinks it's sorcery.
Iron ingots, if you see any. Real tools, if you find a miracle.

topics.speaker: SFVenn
topics.prompt: How does the resonance array work?

responses.text: Crystals vibrate. We amplify the vibration. Reality gets nervous.
Push it too far and reality gets more than nervous. That's Hale's favorite part.

topics.speaker: SFVenn
topics.prompt: What do you think of Hale?

responses.text: Hale plays my generators like a drum. I treat his requests like weather.
Something to complain about, and nothing I can stop.

topics.speaker: SFVenn
topics.prompt: Have you seen any magic here?

responses.text: A fellow in Whiterun froze a puddle by glaring at it. I've stopped asking questions.
And some old court wizard in Windhelm bought our notes. Wuunferth. Built a crystal trap from them.
Keep the fence up, the creatures out, and the scientists alive. In that order.
Some days I'd swap the last two.
Good people. Tired people. Nine of them, on a site that needs thirty.
They didn't sign up for crabs. They signed up for a paycheck and a view.

topics.speaker: SFMoran
topics.prompt: How do you handle the creatures?

responses.text: Zombies are slow. Crabs are fast. Kill the fast ones first.
And never let one onto your face. That's the whole training.
Canisters. The rifts spit them out all over these mountains.
My people haul them in when they can. Some trips, not everyone comes back.

topics.speaker: SFMoran
topics.prompt: What do you think of the scientists?

responses.text: They're smart. Smart people make the biggest messes.
Rusk is all right. He worries. I trust the ones who worry.

topics.speaker: SFMoran
topics.prompt: Can I get into the armory?

responses.text: Not without clearance. And clearance comes from the Director.
You've got clearance. The chest is unlocked. Take what you need.
Readings. Logs. More readings. And I fetch things for Dr. Hale.
Sometimes I fetch Dr. Hale, when the fumes knock him over.
Nervous? Me? I just jump at shadows. The shadows here have teeth.

topics.speaker: SFPell
topics.prompt: Did someone run off with a prototype?

responses.text: Oh. Yes. One of us, a junior like me. Ran toward Riverwood after Incident Seven.
Honestly? Some nights I wish I'd gone too.
Senior researcher in a year. Test Chamber in two. Director in five.
Write that down. You'll want to say you knew me.

topics.speaker: SFHolt
topics.prompt: What do you think of Hale?

responses.text: Talented. Loud. Overdue for retirement, if you ask me. Nobody asks me.
Cold. Loud. Everyone thinks a beard counts as a personality.
Though I'll admit, the mead grows on you.
A saga about a Nord who wrestled a bear to win a bride.
I'm not sure who won. I'm not sure the bear knew either.
Every day. But Riverwood is kind. People share bread without asking why.

topics.speaker: SFMire
topics.prompt: What do the locals say about the crater?

responses.text: They call it the falling star. Some think we're its priests.
A farmer brought us cheese as an offering. We kept the cheese.

topics.speaker: SFKast
topics.prompt: The guards told me to speak with you.

responses.text: Well. You've brought back our missing prototype. Hale will be insufferable.
A junior took it in a panic. How it reached your hands, I won't ask. Yet.
Make yourself useful. Report to Dr. Hale in the Test Chamber.

topics.speaker: SFKast
topics.prompt: The guards told me to speak with you.

responses.text: Director Aurelius Kast. Welcome to Starfall, such as it is.
We're shorthanded. A prototype was stolen, and half my staff jumps at shadows.
If you want to help, report to Dr. Hale in the Test Chamber.

topics.speaker: SFHale
topics.prompt: Director Kast sent me to help you.

responses.text: Fresh hands! Wonderful. I need energy crystals. Three of them.
Embershard Mine near Riverwood is full of them. Bring three back to me.
Look at them glow! These are perfect.
Rusk was asking after you. See him before he chews through his gloves.
Always. But trading with outsiders needs Directorate Clearance.
Get the Director to sign off, and my stock is yours.
Step right up. Crystals, fresh from the crater.

topics.speaker: SFRusk
topics.prompt: Dr. Hale said you wanted to see me.

responses.text: Yes. Quietly, please. My research journal is in Containment Wing B.
It was sealed during Incident Seven. I need it back. Take my keycard.
Be careful in there. Things may still be moving.

topics.speaker: SFRusk
topics.prompt: Tell me again about Wing B.

responses.text: Down the east stairs, past the decontamination showers. The journal is in my old office.
And don't let the Director see you go.
You found it. Thank you. Now you should know what's in it.
Kast ordered Wing B sealed during Incident Seven. Our people were still inside.
Then he buried the report. I signed the false roster. Now you know.
Four researchers and two officers. They knocked on that door for hours.
Because you're not one of us. Kast can't silence you with a transfer.
Go to him. Make him say it out loud.

topics.speaker: SFKast
topics.prompt: Rusk told me about Wing B.

responses.text: So he finally found his courage. Good for him.
Yes. I sealed Wing B. The hosts were at the door. Seconds mattered.
Six lives against the whole site, and perhaps Riverwood. I chose. Now you judge.

children.speaker: SFKast
children.prompt: You left them to die. That's murder.

responses.text: Perhaps it is. I'll carry it either way.
But you've earned the truth, and something more. You now hold Directorate Clearance.
Hale will trade with you, and Moran will open the armory. Use them better than I did.

children.speaker: SFKast
children.prompt: You made a hard choice. I understand.

responses.text: Understanding. I hadn't expected that from anyone.
Then take this as thanks. You now hold Directorate Clearance.
Hale's stock and Moran's armory are open to you. Keep this site honest. I couldn't.
